page: Amazon Web Services i8g.metal-48xl is a storage-optimized bare-metal server powered by AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processors. It features 192 physical cores and 192 vCPUs operating at a dedicated 2.8 GHz frequency, utilizing the arm64 architecture. The system is equipped with 1536.0 GB of DDR5 memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance includes a bundled 45,000 GB NVMe SSD configuration, complemented by a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate top-tier capabilities in multi-core processing and memory throughput. The server achieves top-tier status in stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and large-block memory bandwidth, reaching 871.74 GB/sec for uncached reads and 403.47 GB/sec for writes. Database operations are highly efficient, with Passmark database tests and Redis SET operations both placing in the top 10% of benchmarks, the latter processing 347.98 million operations per second. However, single-core performance and LLM text generation speeds represent notable tradeoffs, scoring in the average and weak-to-poor tiers respectively.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the bare-metal architecture delivers high resource density by combining massive local NVMe storage with a high-count ARM core layout, reducing virtualization overhead. This profile makes the instance highly suitable for large-scale database deployments, high-throughput Redis caching layers, static web serving, and multi-threaded data processing workloads. It is less suited for workloads requiring high single-threaded performance or GPU-accelerated machine learning tasks.
description: Amazon Web Services i8g.metal-48xl is a storage-optimized bare-metal server designed for high-throughput data workloads. Powered by AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processors, it delivers 192 dedicated physical cores on the arm64 architecture, paired with 1536.0 GB of DDR5 memory and a massive 45,000 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The server features a 100 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark data highlights top-tier multi-core CPU performance, exceptional memory bandwidth, and superior database execution speeds, including 347.98 million operations per second in Redis SET tests. Conversely, single-core performance and LLM text generation are moderate to weak. This bare-metal configuration offers high resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for I/O-intensive applications, making it an excellent fit for large-scale databases, high-capacity caching layers, static web serving, and intensive multi-threaded data processing.
